transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Turn off the washing machine immediately using its power button. Do not touch the plug or socket while your hands are wet or if there is standing water near them; instead, go to your consumer unit (fuse box) and switch off the circuit that supplies the kitchen, or unplug the machine only if you can do so completely dry and without stepping in water. Once the power is isolated, place towels under the machine to soak up any remaining water. The most common causes for a leak underneath are a loose pump filter cap, a blocked filter causing overflow, or a split door seal. Please check the small access panel at the bottom front: is the circular filter cap tight and dry, or is it leaking?

ok the filter cap is tight and the bit behind the flap is dry. but I'm standing in socks on the wet floor and the water is right by the socket, should I get out of the water first before going to the fuse box??

Yes, get out of the water immediately and go to your fuse box to switch off the kitchen circuit before doing anything else. Do not touch the plug or socket while wet. Once the power is isolated and you are safe, we need to find where the water is coming from since the filter cap was dry. The most likely cause now is that the drain hose at the back is pushed too far into your wall waste pipe (more than 15cm), causing a blockage and overflow, or the waste pipe itself is blocked. Please check this connection when you can do so safely.
ok I'm going to the fuse box in the hall now, the floor there is dry. should I check the drain hose at the back? I can't pull the machine out on my own, its full of water and really heavy

Yes, please check the drain hose at the back. Since you cannot pull the machine out safely and it is still full of water, we need to determine if the blockage is external (at the wall waste) or internal. Look at where the grey hose goes into your wall waste pipe or sink standpipe: if it is pushed in too far, it can create a vacuum that stops drainage and causes overflow; if the waste pipe itself is blocked, water will back up. If the hose looks clear and the waste pipe isn't full, the leak is likely coming from inside the machine (such as a loose sump hose or pump housing), which would require an engineer to access once the water is removed.
ok I've switched it off at the fuse box. I can't get behind the machine to see the drain hose though, it's too heavy to move on my own. Is there anything else I can check from the front?

Since the filter cap is dry and you cannot safely move the machine to check the rear hose, the water is likely leaking from inside the cabinet—either a loose sump hose or a cracked pump housing. Because there was water near your socket, this appliance must not be used again until a qualified engineer has inspected it for both the leak and any electrical damage. Please arrange for an engineer to come out; they will need to drain the machine and check the internal components.
